hints: Notice the $6.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ boat arrow is the hypotenuse tilted upstream by $\theta$, while the $4.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ water acts left to right.
For zero drift along the banks, the upstream component of the boat must cancel the water speed, so $6.0\sin\theta = 4.0$.
For the speed straight across, use Pythagoras with $6.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ as hypotenuse: $v = \sqrt{6.0^2 - 4.0^2}$.
walkthrough: Draw the vector triangle: boat velocity $6.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ at $\theta$ to the perpendicular, water velocity $4.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ along the river, resultant $v$ perpendicular to the banks.
Resolve perpendicular and parallel to the banks. Parallel components must sum to zero for a perpendicular resultant, so $6.0\sin\theta - 4.0 = 0$.
The $6.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ vector is the hypotenuse, so the across-river resultant is the other short side: $v = 6.0\cos\theta = \sqrt{6.0^2 - 4.0^2}$.
Substitute: $v = \sqrt{36 - 16} = \sqrt{20} \approx 4.47\ \text{m s}^{-1} \approx 4.5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, smaller than $6.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ as expected.
